research_notes:
CATL's largest single-site battery base, in Fuding, Ningde, Fujian, China. Wholly owned by CATL (not a JV). Phase 1 (RMB 17bn) started production December 2021 as a 60 GWh lithium-ion base; four cell factories (No.1-No.4) plus module factories were reported in production by September 2022. Total planned capacity across the base widely reported at 120 GWh (five factory buildings); nameplate_capacity_gwh set to 120 and capacity_by_year_json shows the 60->120 GWh ramp. In May 2026 CATL announced a sixth-phase expansion adding 40 GWh of annual sodium-ion cell capacity (RMB 5bn / ~$735m), which would bring the base's total planned capacity to 149 GWh; that sodium-ion expansion is under construction (~24-month build, targeting ~2028) and is not yet operational, so it is not counted in the operational nameplate here. The overall site is operational (lithium-ion lines running since 2021/2022). Precise plant coordinates not confirmed by a source, so latitude/longitude left null (site is in Fuding, Fujian). Sources: CnEVPost (2021-12-22) on 120 GWh planned / production start; CnEVPost (2026-05-09) and Battery-News (2026-05-11) on the 40 GWh sodium-ion phase-six expansion to 149 GWh total.

Could not confirm a FinDreams (弗迪电池) battery CELL plant in Changzhou. BYD's Changzhou site (华东/East China base, Changzhou National High-Tech Zone, Xinbei district, Jiangsu) is a vehicle assembly base: a ~10bn yuan project signed with the Changzhou government in 2019, design capacity ~400,000 EVs/year (Yuan PLUS, Seagull, Seal), with an associated components industrial park and R&D centre. Vehicle output was ~300,000 units in 2023. Changzhou does NOT appear on multiple compilations of FinDreams' disclosed cell/blade-battery production bases, which instead list Chongqing (Bishan, ~35 GWh), Xi'an (~30), Changsha (Ningxiang, ~20), Guiyang (~20), Bengbu (~20), Wuwei (~20), Jinan (~30), Yancheng/Sheyang (~30), Xiangyang (~30), Fuzhou (~15), Chuzhou (~5), Shenzhen Pingshan (~14), Xining (~24), Huizhou (~2) and the FAW-FinDreams JV in Changchun (15→45 GWh). A 2021 sell-side note ("比亚迪常州基地规划曝光") flagged battery-supply-chain plans around the Changzhou base, and one English aggregator (GoSaveTime) loosely lists Changzhou among BYD "battery and component facilities" — likely conflating pack/component activity with cell manufacturing. No credible source gives a cell-line GWh figure, chemistry, cell format or coordinates for a Changzhou cell plant. Treating this as most likely a vehicle-assembly / component site rather than a cell gigafactory; capacity, chemistry and coordinates left null. announced_year 2019 and start_year ~2021 refer to the vehicle base. Confidence kept low (0.4) given the conflicting aggregator language and the possibility of pack assembly on site. Chinese primary sources (fdbatt.com, dfcfw PDF, stcn, autohome) returned HTTP 403 to the fetch tool; findings rest on aggregated search summaries and the English BYD Wikipedia entry.
